## This work (Р-251 English series, campaign by the model of «Маски», Р-202/Р-228/Р-254)

«The Children of Fear» (Chaosium 2020, 7e; Lynne Hardy with Mike Mason, Sam Riordan and others; optional Pulp Cthulhu notes) goes into the base whole: a 1920s campaign across Asia (September 1923 onward) — Peking, Sian, Tun-huang, the Taklamakan and the Silk Roads, the Northwest Frontier (Chakdara, Peshawar), Bihar (Rajgir, Nalanda, Patna), Kham in Tibet (Derge), Pemakö, Assam. No Russian edition exists (the base, `3_КБ\_Каталог.csv`, `2_Обработка` and the library were checked): the English original is the source, the Russian text is our translation (flag `translated`); official Russian forms of names and terms — glossary `python -B tools/terms.py w1 w2 …` (ONE run for all words) and existing records (Р-184); Hard/Extreme roll = «трудная/чрезвычайная проверка». Work title in Russian: «Дети страха» (`work_title` in the book register); the cult Tokabhaya = «Токабхая» («Дети страха»); the King of Fear = «Царь Страха» (unless the owner decides otherwise — the lead tells you). Tibetan, Sanskrit and Chinese terms (lama, rinpoche, dakini/khandroma, thangka, terma, kangling, damaru, kapala, tsampa, baeyul…) — the book's Glossary p. 24–28 is the reference; one Russian form each, used everywhere, all listed in your coverage file (English → Russian): the page-by-page translation of the book (Р-251, later, by Codex) reuses exactly these forms and your `name.ru`. Place names: the 1920s forms the book uses (Peking, Sian, Tun-huang, Kansu) in `name.en`, the usual Russian form in `name.ru` (Пекин, Сиань, Дуньхуан, Ганьсу), modern and other forms (Beijing, Xi'an, Chang'an, Dunhuang) in `aliases`.

### Source (registered; printed page = physical − 1, i.e. `offset −1`; `pages.py show/grep` take printed pages)

- `children-of-fear-en` — one PDF, 418 physical pages, text layer. NO text layer (only a caption) on: the handouts of Appendix F (p. 363–382 — the handout text is inside the picture; the same picture usually also stands on the chapter page), Appendix C «What Your Investigator Knows» (p. 348–353), the Player Maps (p. 383–398). Read them from page images (`python -B pipeline/source/pages.py image children-of-fear-en <page> --dpi 100`, one page at a time) or OCR (tesseract), and check every OCR line by eye.
- Do NOT edit `pipeline/source/books.json`.

### Fixed ids (all units use them; a reference to a record another unit is still writing is expected to fail `check.py` until that unit lands — list such refs in the report, do not drop them)

- All records live in `kb/books/children-of-fear-en/<kinds>/`, id `children-of-fear-en/<kind>/<slug>`.
- Campaign: `children-of-fear-en/scenario/the-children-of-fear` (unit campaign) — `summary`, `keeper_info` (Agartha and Shambhala, the King of Fear, the Tokabhaya and the Triumvirate, the false ritual and Tenzin Kalsang's sacrifice; the Keeper's Mythos options of «Keeper Considerations» → `advice`), `hook`, `advice` (investigator motivations, dark materials, naming conventions, pulp notes), `steps` = the eight chapters in order with refs to the stage records (say that Chapters 3–5 may be played in any order), `conclusion`, `tables`.
- Stages — scenario records with `part_of` = the campaign and `order`: `children-of-fear-en/scenario/the-city-of-decaying-splendor` (1, peking), `…/to-the-gates-of-the-sun` (2, gates), `…/song-of-the-lost-and-forgotten` (3, song), `…/old-bones` (4, bones), `…/feast-and-famine` (5, feast), `…/liberation` (6, liberation), `…/spirits-of-the-earth` (7, spirits), `…/the-heart-of-the-world` (8, heart). Each stage record: `summary`, `keeper_info`, `hook` («Set Up»), `advice`, `steps` with `refs`, `conclusion` (incl. «Rewards» — Sanity rewards and development), `tables`; scenes have `arc` = {scenario: the stage, part: the book's section heading («Part One: Chang'an», «Start: The Lecture»…), order}; `where`, `participants`, `mechanics`, `outcome`. «Moving On» sections → the last step/scene of the stage with refs to the next stages.
- Slug prefixes of every book-scoped record except named characters and stage records: `campaign-` (campaign), `peking-` (peking), `gates-` (gates), `song-` (song), `bones-` (bones), `feast-` (feast), `liberation-` (liberation), `spirits-` (spirits), `heart-` (heart), `appendix-` (appendix). Slugs from the English names. Handouts by the book's name: «Handout: Decaying Splendor 3» → `peking-handout-3-<slug>`, «Gates 1» → `gates-handout-1-…`, «Song N» → `song-handout-N-…`, «Bones N» → `bones-handout-N-…`, «Feast N» → `feast-handout-N-…`, «Liberation 3a» → `liberation-handout-3a-…`, «Spirits 2b» → `spirits-handout-2b-…`; «What Your Investigator Knows N» (Appendix C) → `<prefix>-knows-N-<slug>` of the unit that owns it (below).
- Characters: named — `children-of-fear-en/character/<english-name>`, no prefix; group profiles and types (Appendix A «Bandit», «Porters», «Six sample pisachas»…) — `children-of-fear-en/character/<prefix>-<slug>` with invented `names` (Р-151). A character is made by the unit whose pages print his statblock first; other units link and send changes (a later statblock as a `variant`, new facts) through proposals. Fixed: peking — `wang-enlai` (p. 36, 48); gates — `langdon-warner` (p. 91), `tenzin-kalsang` (p. 75, 92), `wang-yuanlu`; liberation — the Triumvirate `hine-roimata`, `mariam-sandrine`, `andrei-osipovich-vitsin` (p. 230–231, 263–264), `frank-kingdon-ward` if the box gives him; appendix — the historical figures of Appendix A (`ferdynand-antoni-ossendowski`, `mildred-cable`, `roman-von-ungern-sternberg`, `ekai-kawaguchi`) and the six pre-generated investigators of Appendix G (role `pregen`, «Pulp adjustments» kept in their text; refs from the campaign record are added by the lead). The campaign's «Dramatis Personae» (p. 17–22) text about characters other units make → campaign's proposals.
- Campaign-wide records of unit campaign: organization `children-of-fear-en/organization/campaign-tokabhaya` (the Children of Fear; the Triumvirate described in it, its members linked), creature `children-of-fear-en/creature/campaign-king-of-fear` (Lord of Agartha; the Keeper's options — avatar of Ubbo-Sathla, Nyogtha, Mordiggian, Azathoth's agents… — in its text with refs to `coc:creature:ubbo-sathla`, `coc:creature:nyogtha`, `coc:creature:mordiggian`, `coc:creature:azathoth`, `coc:creature:yog-sothoth`), places `children-of-fear-en/location/campaign-agartha` and `children-of-fear-en/location/campaign-shambhala` (otherworldly kingdoms, `область`, `part_of: null` — book records like the Dreamlands lands, Р-190; places of Shambhala in Chapter 6 go under `campaign-shambhala`), the Glossary (p. 24–28) as a book `rule` record `campaign-glossary`. Chapters link these ids; Sisirama (Chapter 7) is spirits' creature with refs to `campaign-king-of-fear`; the Lords of Shambhala (p. 267) — liberation's record `children-of-fear-en/creature/liberation-lords-of-shambhala`.
- Spells: Appendix B (p. 340–346) is the full text; unit appendix writes it. Existing shared spells — link and send the book's version by proposals (sources, variant text): `coc:spell:alter-weather`, `bind-animal`, `cause-disease`, `curse-folk`, `healing-folk`, `possession`, `telepathy`, `warding-the-eye`, `warmth-of-mind`, `wandering-soul`, `create-gate` (Close Gate is its counterpart — Grep, propose or create), `quicken` (Fleetness of Foot is its variant — Grep). New shared `kb/spells/<slug>.json` (after a Grep shows they do not exist), ids fixed so chapters can link them now: `coc:spell:close-gate`, `the-closing-of-the-way`, `enchant-sacred-instruments`, `mask-of-reason`, `observation-from-afar`, `open-the-gates-of-agartha`, `send-vision`, `summon-bind-khandroma`, `summon-bind-scorpion-demon`, `sword-siddhi`. A spell printed only in a chapter (e.g. the Liturgy of Death ritual, p. 242) — the chapter unit, after a Grep.
- Creatures: shared already (Grep `kb/creatures` first) — `coc:creature:mi-go`, `ghoul`, `rat-thing`, `skeleton`, `scorpion`, `fire-vampire`, `mordiggian`, `ubbo-sathla`, `nyogtha`, `azathoth`, `yog-sothoth`, animals `camel`, `horse`, `bear`, `tiger`, `venomous-snake`…; a known species with its own numbers here (the Abominable Mi-go and the sample migyu, the pisachas as ghouls, the Rat King's rat-things) → book creature with `instance_of` the shared record; unique beings (the scorpion demon, Shri Chitipati, the dakini, the Yakshini and her snakes, the walking portraits, the kueitzumen, Sisirama) → book creatures of the unit whose pages print them.
- Tomes and items: Grep `kb/tomes` and `kb/items` first (e.g. `coc:tome:book-of-dzyan` exists); the ritual implements and relics of a chapter (alms bowls, kangling, damaru, kapalas, khatvanga, rilbus, Ashoka's treasure…) — items of the chapter that makes them, later chapters link them.

### Places (Р-190, Р-209)

- Shared cities `kb/locations/<slug>.json` (id `coc:location:<slug>`, `location_type: город`, `part_of: null`, model `kb/locations/cairo.json`). **Existing — never rewrite, proposals only:** `benares`, `bombay`, `shanghai`, `hong-kong`. Warning: `coc:location:sarnath` is Lovecraft's Dreamlands city — the Indian Sarnath (near Benares) is NOT that record; if you need it, write a draft `sarnath-india` into the new-shared-locations file. **New, each made only by its unit:** `peking` (peking), `sian` and `tun-huang` (gates), `peshawar` and `chakdara` (song; `khotan`, `kashgar`, `turfan` too if the chapter describes them as places, otherwise a draft), `rajgir` (bones), `derge` (feast), `patna` (spirits), `dibrugarh` and `sadiya` (heart, if described). A town en route that a unit needs but nobody owns (Lanchow, Hami, Yarkand, Leh, Gilgit, Srinagar, Rawalpindi, Lahore, Calcutta, Delhi, Darjeeling, Gangtok, Lhasa, Tsetang, Bihar Sharif, Gaya…) — Grep `kb/locations`; if it is missing, write the city draft into `checks/20261127-children-of-fear/new-shared-locations-<unit>.json` (the lead creates it) and give a short line in the stage `steps` meanwhile.
- Wild regions crossed by the journey — book areas (`область`, `part_of: null`) of the unit whose chapter describes them, with the region's places under them: `gates-kansu-corridor`, `song-tarim-basin` (the Taklamakan, the Northern and Southern routes), `song-mountain-passes`, `bones-rajgir-environs` (Vulture's Peak, Sitavana charnel ground), `feast-kham`, `liberation-pemako` (the Valley of the White Ape under it), `spirits-nalanda` (the ruins of Nalanda University), `heart-assam` (Danakosha Lake, the tea gardens, the jungle). Lake Danakosha of Chapter 3 (Swat) and Danakosha Lake of Chapter 8 (Assam) are two places — `song-…` and `heart-…`.
- Under each city — districts by the map, places in the district where they stand; one area «Окрестности <города>» per city for places outside it (book record `<prefix>-<city>-environs`, unless one exists); list captions (`keeper_hint`) neutral — no secrets, clues or outcomes (Р-209).

### Maps (Р-206) and pictures (Р-241, Р-245)

- Every keeper map → `map` record `children-of-fear-en/map/<prefix>-<slug>`: image from the book page (render `pdftoppm -r 150-200`, crop with PIL, save `app/maps/cof-<unit>-<slug>.jpg`, quality 85, ≤ 2000 px wide; a two-page spread — join both halves), `width`/`height`, `location` = the city or area, `shows` = the place, spots on every printed number and label (tesseract `tsv`, each checked by eye on a crop); every key number gets a place record. The player version (Appendix F p. 383–398, «Player version maps») → a second `map` record `<prefix>-<slug>-players` with the same spot targets (model `kb/books/star-on-the-shore-en/maps/rockport-player-map.json`). `sources` of a map — the keeper page and the player page. Keeper maps (index p. 412) and player pages: Central Asia 1923 p. 26–27 / 384–385 (campaign), City of Peking p. 33 / 383 (peking), City of Sian p. 57 / 386 and Kansu Corridor 1923 p. 70 / 387 (gates), Northern and Southern Silk Roads 1924 p. 99 / 388, Mountain Passes p. 110 / 389, City of Peshawar p. 127 / 390, Peshawar Museum 1924 p. 129 / 391 (song), Northern India and the Himalayas 1924 p. 159 / 392 (bones), Northern India and the Tibetan Plateau 1924 p. 199 / 393 (feast), Tibet and the Pemakö Region 1924 p. 234 / 394 (liberation), Nalanda University p. 277 / 395, City of Patna p. 285 / 396, Sitala Devi Mandir p. 291 / 397 (spirits), Assam and surrounding territories p. 307 / 398 (heart).
- Handouts: the text as printed (English, read from the image) + our full translation; the picture (crop of the Appendix F copy, or of the chapter page when that is clearer) to `images` (kind `handout`) through `pipeline/art/add_images.py`; sources — chapter page + Appendix F page (index p. 412 gives both). Portraits, creature art, item pictures — skill `.claude/skills/kb-art/SKILL.md`: mapping `checks/20261127-children-of-fear/art-<unit>.json`, `python -B pipeline/art/add_images.py … --dry-run` then real, apply your proposals (`pipeline/integrate/apply.py`) for your own records; atmosphere pictures (chapter openers «Opposite: …», mood art) → `checks/20261127-children-of-fear/atmosphere-<unit>.json` (the lead merges). Picture file prefix: `cof-<unit>-`.

### Writing and checks

- Statblocks as printed (Р-25); misprints kept as printed, in `errata` (Р-35), an obvious fix in `corrections` (e.g. «OSSENDOWKSI» p. 327); dice `1d6` with lowercase d; distances metric even in quotes (Р-64), money as printed (the book's «About Money» p. 30 — rule record of peking); `axes.era` ["1920s"]; `axes.ruleset` "core" (Pulp Cthulhu options stay in the text of `advice`/«Pulp adjustments»). Sensitive material (human remains, sacrifice, cannibalism) — as printed, with the book's own safety advice kept.
- Real history boxes (Taking Liberties, The Jade Marshal, Sir Marc Aurel Stein, Wellcome's Man in India, The Plant Hunter…) — `rule` records of the chapter or text of the place/character they describe; none dropped (owner's rule: no silent drops).
- Coverage: `checks/20261127-children-of-fear/<unit>.md` — every heading of your pages → record(s), «не взято» with the reason (index, contributor biographies, back cover — say so), misprints, the term list English → Russian. Proposals `checks/20261127-children-of-fear/proposals-<unit>.json`.
- Helper scripts only in `.cache/lead-tools/gen-cof-<unit>/`; paths computed from `__file__` or the repository root; library root from `pipeline/source/library.json`; never hardcoded.
- Memory rule (owner): the PC's RAM must stay below 85 % — never run python processes in parallel; terms in ONE run (`python -B tools/terms.py w1 w2 …` or `--file`); page images one at a time.
- When done: `python -I -B tools/completeness.py --books children-of-fear-en --out checks/20261127-children-of-fear/completeness-<unit>` and `python -I -B tools/scenario_check.py --books children-of-fear-en --out checks/20261127-children-of-fear/scenario-<unit>` (other units' gaps are expected — fix and report only yours); `python -B tools/check.py kb/books/children-of-fear-en` — 0 errors in your files.
- Order: all ten units may run in parallel (by the memory rule); refs between units are fixed above.
